correctness.rationale: The two nested existential quantifiers defining two members of a color may shadow the first variable: transitivity keeps the witnesses in the same class. The two outer witnesses in the global test then distinguish one class from two. In the other direction, match the moved pebble by its color and exact local vector; if no pebble is stationary, h(t)>0 suffices. With a stationary pebble, equality, a different member of its class, and a member of a different class require respectively no new choice, local counts capped at two, and class counts capped at two. This invariant works also on infinite structures. Keeping h(t) classes with exactly t_C survivors of each color is induced and realizes the same profile; conversely every nonzero profile is realized. The all-two profile forces at least 2 times the sum of all local vector weights, namely 2q3^q, in the stated class of structures. The uncolored and one-predicate theory counts and bounds follow. An independent rank-four semantic refinement on all isomorphism types through size six found 8 profiles in 29 models for one color and 124 profiles in 274 models for two colors, with exactly matching truth-signature partitions.
residual_risks: The finite check is corroborative; all sizes and infinite structures are covered by the back-and-forth proof, not by enumeration.
